messages:
Maya: Heads-up — ran a profile sweep on kernel_selector_v2 on a private customer stack and saw a token-level regression on one route. p50 unchanged, but p99 jumped ~35% for long-seq requests. This only repros in their VPC setup where we use the file-based metrics export (air-gapped).

Liam: ugh. do you have the flamegraph or perf sample? could be the new fused-attn kernel falling back to a memcpy path on >2048 seqs.

Maya: Attached perf sample (trimmed) and the token latency histogram from the runtime. snippet:```
# token latency breakdown (route=/chat/long)
token_latency.count{le="0.01"}=12000
token_latency.count{le="0.05"}=15000
token_latency.count{le="0.1"}=15250
token_latency.count{le="+Inf"}=15300
# p99 moved from ~85ms -> ~115ms on this route
```

Samir: quick data point — KV cache hit rate for that customer route is low: kv_cache.hit_rate{route="/chat/long"}=0.62. low hit rate + larger seqs means we do more key lookups and bigger KV deserializations which amplifies memcpy cost.

Anya: hmm. If kv hit is low then batching heuristics could be hurting more than helping. The new sampler tries to batch by seq_len buckets; long-tail spikes create mixed batches => some requests wait and some get stalled by big ones. We should add per-route batching KPIs to the dashboard: batch_size, batch_wait_ms, batch_mixed_ratio.

Liam: agree. also try forcing kernel back to legacy to confirm:```
RUNTIME_KERNSEL=legacy ./redwood-runtime --run-sample --route "/chat/long" --concurrency 8
```
If p99 drops we know selector is the culprit.

Maya: I'll run that. But one wrinkle: their metrics pipeline is air-gapped — we get a tarball of prometheus textfile exports pushed weekly. That means we don't see live token-level breakdowns in Grafana to triage. Any suggestions for adding token-level panels that work in file-export mode?

Anya: You can craft dashboards that rely on the same histogram & labels we expose. For air-gapped flow, two options:
- customer runs our 'metrics-uploader' agent that writes a local file in Prom format (we read it for local dashboards) and they tar it up; or
- they use the textfile collector (node_exporter) + a standardized path so our support scripts can ingest it and render locally.
Either way, dashboard panels should use histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)).

Devon: pushgateway is a footgun here — we should not recommend it. For air-gapped installs we added a small uploader that writes to /var/lib/redwood/metrics/prom-text-YYYYMMDD.prom and a helper to convert to a single scrapeable file. I can upstream instructions to the private docs.

Samir: also flagging kv shards retention — customer is on default low-retention (30s) which hurts long chats. Increasing kv.retention_ms to 120000 improved local repro hit_rate -> 0.82 and p99 dropped ~18%.

Maya: helpful — thanks. Plan: 1) I'll reproduce with RUNTIME_KERNSEL=legacy and post perf flamegraph. 2) Anya to draft token-level dashboard panels for file-export use. 3) Samir to try kv.retention increase on repro and share results. 4) Devon to add private doc snippet warning about pushgateway.

Liam: if you confirm selector is the issue we should add a runtime flag to prefer legacy for routes with high seq variance while we fix kernel_selector heuristics. small patch can gate selector by route label + seq_variance threshold.

infra-bot: deploy queued: runtime/canary v2026.2.3 -> private-canary (triggered by Maya)

Maya: will post results in this thread after the runs. thanks all :thumbsup:
